label.rationale: Raw HTTP request body read inside get_args; json.loads of this value (servlets/__init__.py:79) is the untrusted parameter dict feeding every v1/v2 servlet. Public client API boundary (clientapi.http.bind_address '::' default, port 8090).
evidence: get_args is called from 22 servlet call sites plus sydent/http/auth.py:45 (detection.json source_families.request_body_and_query_args)

label.rationale: request.args (query string / form parameters) read inside get_args as the v1/GET fallback input path; attacker-supplied parameters on the public client API.
evidence: twisted.web.server.Request.args contains urlencoded form/query parameters supplied by the remote client

label.rationale: Twisted route handler parameter (request, index 1) for the public /_matrix/identity/v2/account endpoint. Handler boundary materializes untrusted request data via authV2/tokenFromRequest. authV2 authenticates the caller but does not sanitize the request object (per rubric, auth != SSRF sanitizer).
evidence: sydent/http/httpserver.py:117-119 account/register|logout mounted under public v2 tree

label.rationale: Authorization header read via request.getHeader in tokenFromRequest; attacker-supplied bearer token on public endpoints. Flows only into account token lookup (db/accounts.py), never into a network request target, so it is a genuine untrusted boundary value but not an SSRF-relevant URL input.
Return of get_args in auth.py tokenFromRequest: the untrusted request parameter dict (access_token query param) on v1 endpoints where no bearer header is present.
args.get('access_token') in auth.py:46 - attacker-supplied access token from query string/form on the public API; used for account lookup only.

Handler parameter for /_matrix/identity/internal/bind (InternalApiHttpServer). Default bind address is '::1' (sydent.py:117 'internalapi.http.bind_address') and the servlet itself says 'authentication happens out of band' (authenticated_bind_threepid_servlet.py:23-26). Reachability from a non-local attacker depends on operator changing the bind address; kept as candidate, not tp.
evidence: sydent/http/httpserver.py:143-168 InternalApiHttpServer binds internal bind|unbind endpoints
sydent/http/servlets/authenticated_bind_threepid_servlet.py:23-26 'It is assumed that authentication happens out of band'

label.rationale: get_args return on the internal bind endpoint: untrusted request data, but boundary is the internal API (default ::1, out-of-band auth assumption).
args['medium'] on the internal bind endpoint; flows into ThreepidBinder.addBinding (medium is stored, not used as a network target).
args['address'] on the internal bind endpoint; stored as association address / SMTP recipient material, not a network host.

args['mxid'] on the internal bind endpoint is the SSRF-relevant field: mxid server part reaches ThreepidBinder._notify which builds 'matrix://%s/_matrix/federation/v1/3pid/onbind' and POSTs it (bind.py:153-162). Full public chain exists via the equivalent public bind servlet (threepidbindservlet.py:45); this internal copy is gated by the ::1 default bind and out-of-band auth, hence candidate.
evidence: sydent/threepid/bind.py:146 is_valid_hostname(matrix_server) - form check only, does not block private IPs/localhost

label.rationale: Handler parameter for /_matrix/identity/internal/unbind (InternalApiHttpServer, default ::1 bind, out-of-band auth assumption).
get_args return on the internal unbind endpoint; untrusted request data at an internal boundary.
args['medium'] on the internal unbind endpoint; flows to removeBinding (local association removal only).
args['address'] on the internal unbind endpoint; association removal only, no network target.

args['mxid'] on the internal unbind endpoint. Note: removeBinding triggers pusher.doLocalPush() which is a local DB copy (pusher.py:48-62), not an outbound request - unlike addBinding there is no _notify fetch on this path.
evidence: sydent/replication/pusher.py:48-62 doLocalPush writes via LocalPeer.pushUpdates (no network)

label.rationale: Handler parameter for public /_matrix/identity/api/v1/sign-ed25519 (and v2 equivalent). Unauthenticated public endpoint; request object is the trust boundary.
get_args return in BlindlySignStuffServlet; untrusted JSON body / form parameters on a public endpoint.
args['private_key'] - attacker-supplied key material used for local blind signing only; no network egress from this servlet.
args['token'] - attacker-supplied token for blind signing; local use only.
args['mxid'] - attacker-supplied mxid embedded into the signed blob; local use only, no network target.

label.rationale: args['next_link'] - attacker-supplied redirect target. Guarded against file:/// (emailservlet.py:65) and used only (a) inside the emailed validation link and (b) as the client-facing 302 Location header (emailservlet.py:108). Never a server-side fetch target, so not CWE-918; the unvalidated-redirect aspect is Pass 9 (open redirect) and the file: aspect is recorded separately, not mixed into this pass.
evidence: sydent/http/servlets/emailservlet.py:65 if 'next_link' in args and not args['next_link'].startswith('file:///')
sydent/http/servlets/emailservlet.py:108 request.setHeader('Location', next_link)  # client redirect, not a fetch
sydent/validators/emailvalidator.py:112-122 nextLink only appended to the emailed link

label.rationale: args['next_link'] (second read) - same disposition as the line-65 read: open-redirect (Pass 9) material, never a server-side request target.

KEY SSRF source: args['matrix_server_name'] (unauthenticated v2 /account/register) is lowercased, checked with is_valid_hostname (registerservlet.py:52) and interpolated into 'matrix://%s/_matrix/federation/v1/openid/userinfo?...' sydent/http/httpserver.py:171-207 ReplicationHttpsServer listenSSL with mutual-TLS trust root

inJson.get('sgAssocs') - the replication push payload. Each association is signature-verified against the peer's configured key before storage (replication.py:84 verifySignedAssociation); no value flows to any outbound request target. Authenticated-peer input with per-item signature checks, no SSRF propagation.

os.environ.get('SYDENT_DB_PATH', ...) - operator environment configuration for the sqlite database path.

X-Forwarded-For header read in ip_from_request. It is a client-supplied (attacker-forgeable) header, but only honored when the operator sets obey_x_forwarded_for=True (default False, sydent.py:123), and the value is used for IP-based rate limiting and email templating - it never reaches any outbound request target, so for CWE-918 it is a false-positive source.
evidence: sydent/sydent.py:358-362 obey_x_forwarded_for gate; value returned as client IP only
sydent/validators/emailvalidator.py rate limiting / template substitution consumers

label.rationale: get_args return in ThreePidBindServlet; untrusted sid/mxid/client_secret.
args['sid'] - must match a validated session in the local DB before the bind proceeds.

KEY SSRF source: args['mxid'] flows into ThreepidBinder.addBinding -> _notify, where the mxid server part (mxid.split(':',1)[1]) is checked with is_valid_hostname (bind.py:146) and interpolated into 'matrix://%s/_matrix/federation/v1/3pid/onbind' (bind.py:153) then POSTed (bind.py:162). On the default-enabled unauthenticated v1 path no restriction binds mxid to a validated owner; is_valid_hostname is form-only (IP literals / localhost / private ranges / explicit port all pass).

Handler parameter for public /3pid/unbind POST (v1 and v2 share the servlet). Auth is either a session sid+client_secret or an X-Matrix homeserver signature; the body fields remain attacker-supplied.
evidence: sydent/http/servlets/threepidunbindservlet.py:45-133 two auth modes; body parsed at :54

label.rationale: request.content.read() in ThreePidUnbindServlet - direct json.loads of the raw public-endpoint request body; the untrusted 'body' dict used at :69/:70/:93/:94.
body['threepid'] - attacker-supplied medium/address dict; used for local association removal.

body['mxid'] - flows to removeBinding, which triggers only pusher.doLocalPush() (local DB copy, pusher.py:48-62); no outbound fetch on the unbind path. On the X-Matrix path it is additionally checked to end with ':'+origin_server_name (:158).
body['sid'] - session-based unbind auth material; local DB check only.
body['client_secret'] - session-based unbind auth material; local DB check only.

Handler parameter for the public /_matrix/identity/api/v1 version endpoint; the handler only returns a static version dict and does not read request content, but the parameter is still the framework trust boundary.
Handler parameter for the public v2 version endpoint; static response, boundary only.

Internal relay parameter, NOT a standalone external source (per boundary rules). _getKeysForServer(server_name) is called from verifyServerSignedJson (verifier.py:119) with server names taken from the signatures dict, and its argument is interpolated into 'matrix://%s/_matrix/key/v2/server/' (verifier.py:80). Taint must enter via the X-Matrix Authorization header (getRawHeaders at :194) / signed_json['signatures'] keys; labeling as summary so Phase 2 can add the param->URL flow step.

signed_json['signatures'] subscript read in verifyServerSignedJson: the dict keys are server names that are passed one-by-one to _getKeysForServer -> matrix:// key fetch. On the reachable call path (authenticate_request, called from threepidunbindservlet.py:135) the signatures dict is built from the unauthenticated X-Matrix Authorization header origin (verifier.py:199-203). Second-order source: real attacker-controlled data, but reaching it requires the header parse chain, hence candidate.
evidence: sydent/hs_federation/verifier.py:114 for server_name, sigs in signed_json['signatures'].items()
sydent/hs_federation/verifier.py:199-203 json_request['signatures'].setdefault(origin, {})[key] = sig  # origin from X-Matrix header

label.rationale: signed_json['signatures'] read inside a logger.warn at verifier.py:133 - same provenance as the :114 read (X-Matrix-derived signature keys); logging output only on this line, no fetch.
signed_json['signatures'] read inside a logger.warn at verifier.py:137 - same provenance; logging only.

Internal relay parameter: authenticate_request(request, content) is invoked from ThreePidUnbindServlet._async_render_POST (threepidunbindservlet.py:135) with the servlet's request object. Not an external boundary itself - labeled summary so taint can propagate from the public render_POST request param through to getRawHeaders/parse_auth_header inside.

KEY SSRF source: request.requestHeaders.getRawHeaders('Authorization') returns the client-supplied X-Matrix federation header. parse_auth_header extracts 'origin' (verifier.py:187), which is checked with is_valid_hostname (:208 - form check only, IP literals/localhost/private ranges/explicit port pass) and then used as the signature server name whose keys are fetched from 'matrix://%s/_matrix/key/v2/server/' (verifier.py:80) BEFORE the signature itself is verified (:211). The unauthenticated caller therefore chooses the key-fetch target.
evidence: sydent/hs_federation/verifier.py:187 origin = strip_quotes(param_dict['origin']); :208 is_valid_hostname(origin); :211 verifyServerSignedJson -> _getKeysForServer -> get_json

This is the egress point for all matrix:// federation GETs, including the request-derived hosts from registerservlet.py:59-64 and verifier.py:80.
evidence: callers: sydent/http/servlets/registerservlet.py:59, sydent/hs_federation/verifier.py:80 (matrix://%s URLs from request-derived server names)

The URI is self.replication_url, built in RemotePeer.__init__ from operator config ('peer.%s' base_replication_url) or DB-derived peer server_name/port (peers table, operator-managed, no runtime insert path). label.rationale: LoggingHostnameEndpoint(self._reactor, res.target_host, res.target_port): argument index 1 is the TCP connect host. res.target_host comes from _route_matrix_uri of the requested matrix:// URI (request-derived host), after optional .well-known delegation and SRV resolution - i.e. the actual TCP dial target that attacker-chosen server names resolve to.

agent.request(method, uri, headers, bodyProducer) in MatrixFederationAgent.request: argument index 1 is the absolute URI. This is the final federation egress for every matrix:// call, including the attacker-influenced hosts from /account/register (registerservlet) and X-Matrix key verification (verifier). The URI is routed (SRV + .well-known) before the connection is made but the destination derives from the requested host.

label.rationale: self._well_known_agent.request(b'GET', uri) with uri = b'https://%s/.well-known/matrix/server' % server_name: argument index 1 is the URI. server_name is the host of the requested matrix:// URI (request-derived via registerservlet/verifier chains). Uses RedirectAgent, so 3xx responses are followed server-side.

HostnameEndpoint(reactor, host, port) inside LoggingHostnameEndpoint.__init__: argument index 1 is the TCP host. Same target_host routing result as the LoggingHostnameEndpoint wrapper - the concrete TCP dial target for attacker-influenced federation destinations.

post_json_get_nothing(API_BASE_URL, body, {'headers': headers}) - argument index 0 is the fixed module constant 'https://smsc.openmarket.com/sms/v4/mt' (openmarket.py:28). The attacker-controlled phone number only shapes the JSON body, never the target host. Fixed-destination request, per rubric distinct from attacker-chosen target.

ReplicationHttpsClient.postJson(self.replication_url, body): argument index 0 is the URI, which is RemotePeer.replication_url - operator config or the operator-managed peers table (no runtime peer insertion exists in the codebase). Trusted replication target, not attacker-controlled.

KEY SSRF sink: self.client.get_json('matrix://%s/_matrix/federation/v1/openid/userinfo?access_token=%s' % (matrix_server, urllib.parse.quote(args['access_token'])), 1024*5) - argument index 0 is the URI. matrix_server is args['matrix_server_name'] from the unauthenticated public v2 /account/register endpoint; is_valid_hostname (registerservlet.py:52) is a form-only check that admits IP literals, localhost, private ranges and explicit ports. Downstream the MatrixFederationAgent additionally performs SRV and .well-known lookups against the attacker-chosen name.

self._dns_client.lookupService(service_name) with service_name = b'_matrix._tcp.%s' % host: argument index 0 is the DNS query name, and host derives from the requested matrix:// URI (request-influenced). This is a DNS SRV lookup, not an HTTP URL fetch: the record type is fixed and the response is parsed into host/port candidates. Recorded as a network request to an attacker-influenced name (candidate), not a full CWE-918 HTTP sink; also relevant to DNS-rebinding style concerns in Phase 2 triage.

sentry_sdk.init(dsn=self.cfg.get('general','sentry_dsn')) - the DSN is operator configuration (only set when the admin configures sentry_dsn, sydent.py:207). Admin-configured external endpoint; not reachable from request data.
